The full JAD stack runs {count} Docker C: The full JAD stack runs {count} Docker Compose services (profiles included) across six layers: infrastructure (Traefik, PostgreSQL, Vault, NATS, Keycloak), EDC-V / DCore (Control Plane, dual Data Planes), Identity (Identity Hub, Issuer Service), CFM (Tenant/Provision Managers, 4 background agents), Application (Neo4j, Proxy, UI), and a static GitHub Pages export. The same topology is deployed to Azure Container Apps at {host} (21 Container Apps and 9 Container Apps jobs on 2026-10-04, see ADR-012). Arrows show runtime dependencies.
The Azure deployment runs Monday to Frid: The Azure deployment runs Monday to Friday, 05:00 to 18:00 UTC, and is stopped outside those hours (ADR-053). Stopping is a real stop through the Container Apps API, not scale-to-zero, because nearly every service is called by another one and would never reach zero replicas. The UI is the exception: it sleeps at zero replicas, wakes for a visitor and serves an offline notice that links the static export.
Berlin public holidays skip the start. T: Berlin public holidays skip the start. The catalog crawler runs in office hours only. A night or weekend session holds the stack with the repository variable LIVE_DEMO_HOLD_UNTIL; see the off-hours runbook.

The Dataspace Protocol (DSP) governs how: The Dataspace Protocol (DSP) governs how data holders and data users negotiate access to health datasets. The EHDS regulation adds HDAB approval as a pre-requisite for data permit issuance before contract negotiation can proceed.
DSP contract negotiation as a sequence d: DSP contract negotiation as a sequence diagram: the user queries the catalogue, applies to the access body and receives the permit as a credential, then negotiates the contract with the holder, who verifies the permit and evaluates the policy before agreeing and transferring the data

The Decentralized Claims Protocol (DCP): The Decentralized Claims Protocol (DCP) manages identity, credentials, and trust. Identity Hub stores DIDs and Verifiable Credentials, the Issuer Service mints EHDS-specific credentials, and Keycloak provides SSO/OIDC authentication.

The hub and the EU's Simpl-Open middlewa: The hub and the EU's Simpl-Open middleware stand on the same foundation: both run Eclipse EDC connectors, speak the Dataspace Protocol and admit participants with credentials from an authority they trust. The hub joins a Simpl data space as an EDC connector outside the Simpl-Open agent (<adr>ADR-064</adr>) and brings what health adds on top: FHIR and OMOP semantics, data permits, the right to opt out (Art. 71), fees and the gate in front of the secure processing environments.
